scale_008:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare interview stage templates for our hiring pipeline, ahead of my review and sign-off. Do not create, publish, or activate anything in our ATS without my explicit approval — this is an assist step only.

First, ask me for: (1) the ATS or hiring tool we use (e.g. Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, or a spreadsheet), (2) the list of role types we're hiring for (e.g. Software Engineer, Sales, Customer Support, Product Manager), and (3) any existing interview stage conventions or competencies we already use, if any.

Once I provide these, draft a proposed interview stage sequence for each role type. For each role, include: stage name and order (e.g. Recruiter Screen, Hiring Manager Screen, Technical/Skills Assessment, Panel/Onsite Interviews, Culture/Values Interview, Final Debrief), the purpose of each stage, suggested interviewer role (recruiter, hiring manager, peer, senior leader), and which competencies or scorecard criteria that stage should evaluate. Base this on standard hiring practice patterns, but flag clearly where judgment calls are needed (e.g. whether a technical role needs a take-home vs. live coding stage, or whether a culture-fit stage should be separate or merged).

Organize the output as a clear per-role table or list so I can quickly review and edit. Do not enter these stages into the ATS or notify any interviewers yet.

When the draft is ready, present it to me along with a short checklist of decisions I need to make per role (e.g. number of stages, which competencies to prioritize, interviewer assignments). Then stop for human sign-off — do not configure, save, or activate any stage in our hiring tool until I explicitly approve the final version role by role.

scale_008:n2.prompt:
You are helping me create job postings in Lever as part of our multi-role hiring pipeline setup. Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have: (1) the list of open roles, including title, department, and location for each; (2) job description content or bullet points for responsibilities/requirements per role (or ask me to supply/approve draft copy you write); (3) hiring team members and their roles (recruiter, hiring manager, interviewers) to associate with each posting; (4) compensation range or salary info if we disclose it; (5) which pipeline/stage each posting should route candidates into; and (6) whether each posting should include our standard diversity/EEO disclosure language.

Using our configured Lever credentials, for each role: draft the job posting content (title, department, location, description, requirements, salary if provided), and prepare it in Lever as a draft or unpublished posting — do not publish or make any posting publicly live. Associate the correct hiring team members and pipeline stage with each draft. If Lever requires selecting an existing job requisition or creating one, prepare the requisition details as well, but leave it unapproved/unpublished.

Because a human must explicitly approve before any changes are applied, once all draft postings are prepared, compile a summary listing each role, its draft link or identifier in Lever, assigned hiring team, and current status (draft, awaiting approval). Present this summary to me for review and then stop for human sign-off — do not publish, activate, or submit any posting yourself. Wait for my explicit approval before taking any further action in Lever.

scale_008:n3.prompt: You are helping me configure scorecard templates in Lever for our multi-role hiring pipeline. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available via my configured credentials, including: (1) the list of open roles or role families we're hiring for (e.g., Engineering, Sales, Design), (2) the interview stages/panel structure for each role, (3) the core competencies, skills, and values we want scored at each stage (or ask if I want you to draft standard ones based on the role titles), (4) whether we want a shared 'core values' section on every scorecard plus role-specific sections, and (5) any diversity-tracking or structured-rating requirements (e.g., numeric scale, required written justification, blind review notes) that must be reflected in the template design. Using this, draft a scorecard template proposal for each role/stage combination in Lever's scorecard template format, including: template name, associated job posting(s) or stage, list of attributes/questions to be scored, rating scale, and any required fields. Do not create, edit, publish, or apply any scorecard template in Lever — only prepare the drafts and a clear checklist showing which templates will be created or modified, what fields each contains, and which roles/stages they attach to. Present this checklist and draft content to me for review. Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied in Lever, you must stop for human sign-off after presenting the drafts — do not submit, save, or activate anything on my behalf. Report back with the full draft templates, the checklist, and a clear note that you are awaiting my approval before any changes are made in Lever.

scale_008:n4.prompt:
You are helping me configure the offer approval workflow in Lever as part of our hiring pipeline setup. Lever is our confirmed ATS for this step—do not consider alternatives.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available via my configured credentials or workspace context, specifically: (1) the list of roles/levels that require offer approval (e.g., all roles, or only certain seniority levels), (2) the names/titles of approvers for each stage (e.g., hiring manager, department head, finance, CEO) and the order they should approve in, (3) any dollar-amount or role-based thresholds that change the approval chain, and (4) whether approvals should be sequential or parallel.

Once I provide this, draft the full offer approval workflow configuration for Lever: define the approval stages, the named approvers per stage, the sequence/parallel logic, any conditional branching by role or compensation threshold, and notification settings for approvers. Also prepare a short checklist summarizing exactly what will be created or changed in Lever's offer settings, so I can review it before anything goes live.

Do not create, save, publish, or activate any workflow, approver assignment, or setting inside Lever. Do not submit or approve anything on my behalf. Prepare everything as a clear, ready-to-apply draft (including field-by-field values matching Lever's offer approval configuration screens) and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the full draft workflow structure, the approver list and sequence, any thresholds/conditions applied, and the pre-filled checklist ready for me to review and manually apply in Lever myself.

scale_008:n5.prompt:
You are helping me connect {{vendor}} (our scheduling tool) for the hiring pipeline so interviewers can share live-availability booking links for candidate interviews. Before starting, ask me for: (1) our {{vendor}} account login/workspace details (I will use my configured credentials), (2) which interviewer calendars need to be connected (Google, Outlook, and/or Apple), (3) the event types we need (e.g., 30-min phone screen, 60-min panel interview, onsite loop) with their durations, locations, and any custom screening questions, (4) our working-hours/availability preferences including date overrides and out-of-office periods, (5) whether inbound interview requests should round-robin across a hiring team with any weighting, and (6) which CRM/ATS or automation tool (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot, Zapier) should receive booking data.

Then, using the {{vendor}} dashboard: draft the proposed event types with names, durations, locations, and confirmation rules; draft the availability schedule per interviewer; prepare the round-robin/team distribution configuration if requested; and prepare the integration mapping to the CRM/ATS or automation tool, listing exactly what data will sync (candidate name, time, event type, etc.).

Important: connecting a calendar requires an OAuth authorization grant tied to a specific employee's identity — this remains a human step. Do not attempt to authorize, click through, or approve any calendar connection consent screen yourself.

Once everything is drafted, compile a clear summary: proposed event types, availability rules, team routing logic, and integration mapping. Present this to me and then stop for human sign-off — I will personally review and complete the OAuth authorization and any final approval before changes go live.

scale_008:n6.prompt:
You are helping me configure hiring-related channels in {{vendor}}, our team-chat tool, as part of setting up our multi-role hiring pipeline. This step requires my explicit approval before any changes are applied to our workspace, so you must prepare everything but stop before creating anything live.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: the list of open roles/hiring pipelines we need channels for (e.g., role names or req IDs), our naming convention preference (e.g., hiring-<role>), whether channels should be public or private, and whether any external partners (e.g., recruiting agencies or contractors) need guest access to specific channels.
2. Using your configured credentials, draft the exact channel creation commands needed, one per role, using the format: buzz channels create --name "hiring-<role>" --type stream --visibility <open|private> — filling in the actual role names and visibility settings I provide.
3. For each channel, note in your draft whether it should have membership controls (who should be invited: hiring manager, recruiter, interviewers) and whether guest/external access is needed, and how that access should be scoped (limited to that channel only).
4. Compile a clear checklist showing: channel name, visibility, intended members, and guest-access notes for each role.
5. Do NOT run the creation commands or invite anyone yet — present the full checklist and draft commands to me for review.

When done, report back with the complete list of proposed channels, their settings, and membership/guest-access plans, and then stop for human sign-off. I will review and confirm before you proceed to actually create the channels or invite members.

scale_008:n7.prompt:
You are helping me set up diversity tracking in Lever for our hiring pipeline. Diversity data collection has legal/compliance sensitivity, so you must prepare everything but NOT apply any changes in Lever until I explicitly approve.

First, ask me for anything missing: (1) which jurisdictions/countries our roles are hiring in (this affects what EEO/diversity questions are legally permitted or required), (2) whether we want candidate-facing self-identification surveys (e.g., voluntary EEO-style questions on race, gender, veteran/disability status) or only internal source/pipeline diversity metrics, (3) any existing diversity question set or company policy language to reuse, (4) which roles/postings this should apply to (all open reqs or specific ones), and (5) confirmation that you have configured access to our Lever account.

Using this, draft a complete diversity tracking configuration for Lever: the specific survey questions and answer options to add (respecting 'prefer not to answer' options), where in the candidate flow they'd be collected (e.g., application form vs. separate anonymous survey), how responses would be kept anonymized/aggregated and excluded from hiring manager/interviewer views, and how the resulting data would be reported (e.g., pipeline funnel by demographic category). Also note any Lever settings or permissions changes required to enable this.

Produce a clear written summary of the exact configuration you intend to apply in Lever, including question text, options, visibility/anonymization settings, and scope (which pipelines). Do not create, edit, or activate anything in Lever yet — stop for human sign-off. Report back the full draft configuration and wait for my explicit approval before making any changes.
